title: Stork Aerial Photography Rig — Wind & Ballistics Simulator
description: A steampunk camera is mounted beneath a flying stork via a pendulum tether. The user adjusts wind speed, wind direction, tether length, stork altitude, and flight velocity to stabilize the swinging camera over a ground target. Once parameters are dialed in, the user triggers a photo capture that freezes the scene and scores accuracy based on the camera's angular deviation from vertical at the moment of capture.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (importmap with cdn.jsdelivr.net) that loads 'shared_assets/stork.glb' and 'shared_assets/steampunk_camera.glb' via GLTFLoader. Scene setup: a large ground plane with a bright red circular target (radius 1) at the origin, soft directional light plus ambient light, and a sky-blue background. The stork flies in a circular orbit around the target at a configurable radius. The steampunk camera hangs below the stork on a visible line (THREE.Line) acting as a rigid pendulum. Implement simplified 2D pendulum physics: the camera swings based on centripetal acceleration from the stork's circular motion and a configurable horizontal wind force vector. Gravity pulls the camera downward; damping is minimal so the pendulum visibly oscillates. Provide an HTML/CSS control panel with these interactive parameters: (1) Wind Speed slider 0-20 m/s, (2) Wind Direction slider 0-360 degrees, (3) Tether Length slider 2-8 units, (4) Stork Altitude slider 5-20 units, (5) Stork Flight Speed slider 0.5-3.0 rad/s. Each slider must validate min/max and display its current numeric value. Add a 'Capture Photo' button that: freezes the simulation, computes the pendulum's angular deviation from perfectly vertical in degrees, draws a dotted line from the camera to the ground showing where it points, and displays a score overlay (0-100 where 100 means perfectly vertical, i.e., directly over the target). Add a 'Reset' button to resume simulation. The main Three.js camera should be positioned at (25, 15, 25) looking at the origin with OrbitControls. Scale both models so the stork wingspan is roughly 4 units and the steampunk camera is roughly 0.5 units. Animate the stork with a slight banking angle matching its turn radius. The pendulum physics must update each frame using dt from the clock, applying wind as a constant lateral force and centripetal force from circular motion. Display a real-time readout of current swing angle in degrees on the HUD.
